Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: February 3, 2025 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval of Contracts in excess of $5 Million Purpose of Submittal: The purpose of this action item is to seek Board of Trustees approval, under the Policy on Approval and Execution of Contracts and Other Binding Documents, of: 1.
A change order to a contract with First Transit Inc. for campus shuttle services.
This is a time and material contract based on usage throughout the year .
The current contract expires 06/30/25 and the University of Rhode Island is seeking to exercise the renewal option and extend it for two years.
Based on current usage , the University anticipates needing an additional $3.6M to be added to the current Purchase Order (PO) value of $9.6 million.
The proposed increase does not materially change the contract and is based on anticipated increased usage and fuel consumption. 2.

A change order to a contract with marketing firm Katie Schibler & Associates, LLC, (KSA) that extends the contract for an additional five (5) months and increases the total obligation by an estimated $500,000.
This increase and extension does not materially change the nature of the contract.
Recommendation: In the case of First Transit Inc, the extension and increase are part of the original contract renewal options .
This change order is in line with the annual usage and prior spend of this contract and therefore the recommendation is to approve this change order.
KSA is a time and materials contract for media campaigns, marketing and advertising.
The contract is being extended while the solicitation and award of a new contract is in process.
It is also anticipated that some transition time will be necessary should there be a change in vendor.
This increase includes the previously Board of Trustees approved (February 16, 2024) costs for marketing and communications services for Human Resources and the Graduate School, both of which were previously under separate contracts.

Points to Consider: Each of the above contracts represents ongoing support services that are part of the current operations of the campus. A-2 APPENDIX A INFORMATION RELATING TO THE UNIVERSITY OF RHODE ISLAND XX, xx, 2025 Rhode Island Health and Educational Building Corporation 33 Broad Street, Suite 200 Providence, Rhode Island 02903 Dear Members of the Corporation: The University of Rhode Island (the “University” or “URI”) is pleased to submit the following information.
This letter and the information contained herein are submitted to the Rhode Island Health and Educational Building Corporation (“RIHEBC”) for inclusion in its Official Statement relating to its Higher Education Facility Revenue Bonds, University of Rhode Island Educational and General Revenue Issue, Series 20xx (The Series 20xx Bonds).
OVERVIEW OF THE UNIVERSITY OF RHODE ISLAND The University had its beginning as the State Agricultural School chartered in 1888.
The federal Morrill Act of 1862 provided the framework within which the school became the land-grant institution of the State of Rhode Island (the “State”) and in 1892, the school became the Rhode Island College of Agricultural and Mechanic Arts.
The first class of 17 members was graduated two years l ater.

In 1909 the name of the College was changed to Rhode Island State College and the program of study was revised and expanded.
In 1951, the college became known as the University of Rhode Island by act of the State’s General Assembly.
The University of Rhode Island is the S tate’s flagship land and sea grant research institution, with a commitment to urban initiatives.
A student-centered research institution, URI actively partners with other organizations globally and locally to advance knowledge and t o develop informed residents and leaders.
URI is committed to high -quality education, community engagement, and solving the world’s most important challenges.
Situated on the traditional land and territories of the Narragansett Nation and the Niantic People, URI strives to create a diverse and inclusive environment for researchers, teachers, learners, and community members.
URI’s Strategic Plan, Focus URI 2023-2033, lays out the strategic vision for the University for the next decade, outlining four strategic priorities and the actions the University will take to achieve them:

A-3 Strategic Priority 1: Broaden the University’s impact through a reinvigorated commitment to its land- and sea-grant missions and the State of Rhode Island Strategic Priority 2: Enhance student achievement by cultivating an engaged and inclusive learning environment Strategic Priority 3: Foster an inclusive, people-centered culture Strategic Priority 4: Implement leading-edge administrative and financial systems and practices to power the University of the future The University’s main campus in Kingston, RI encompasses approximately 1,400 acres in Kingston, 30 miles south of Providence in the nor theastern metropolitan corridor between New York and Boston.
The 165-acre Narragansett Bay Campus (the “Bay Campus”), located six miles to the east overlooking the west passage of the Narragansett Bay, is home to the Graduate School of Oceanography , and the Ocean Engineering Department of the College of Engineering, and the College of Environment and Life Sciences.
In Providence, the University offers degree programs and non- credit courses and workshops in various locations.

In the western section of the State, 20 miles from Kingston, the 2,300 acres of woods, fields, streams and ponds on the W.
Alton Jones Campus are the site of research by various principal investigators.
The University offers degree programs through the doctoral level.
The University had a combined graduate, undergraduate and dual high school enrollment headcount of 14,452 students for the fall 2023 official reporting.
First year applications for fall 2023 were once again at record levels with 25,391 applications.
GOVERNANCE The Board of Governors for Higher Education became the governing body for the University in 1981, until the Board of Education assumed governance in January 2013.
In 2014, the Board of Education created two councils, including the Council on Postsecondary Education (the “Council”) which exercised oversight of the University, Rhode Island College (“RIC”), and the Community College of Rhode Island (“CCRI”).
On February 1, 2020, governance of the University was transferred to the newly constituted Board of Trustees for the University of Rhode Island (the “Board of Trustees” or the “URI Board”), whose purpose is the oversight of the University .

The Board of Education and the Council will continue to provide oversight for RIC and CCRI .
The URI Board assumed all the powers and duties with respect to the University formerly assigned to the Board of Education and the Council.
The State continues to oversee State funding of higher education, approve borrowing and drive education policy.
The University is held to meeting performance measures required by the State .
The new organizational structure for URI did not materially change the funding or financing arrangements of the State's three public higher education institutions, except in that the URI Board of Trustees has final approval of tuition and mandatory fee rates.
The new URI Board continues to share responsibility for its portion of previously issued bonds for the State’s colleges, which include debt issued by all three public higher institutions in the State: URI, Rhode Island College, and the Community College of Rhode Island.
The enabling legislation creating the Board of Trustees is codified in Rhode Island General Laws Title 16, Chapter 32.

A-4 The Trustees were originally appointed with staggered terms to ensure continuity on the Board.
On an annual basis, trustees are considered for appointment and reappointment by the Governor and are confirmed by the State legislature by the end of each legislative session, typically by June.
Three-year terms will again be staggered, as shown by the term expiration dates of those Trustees who have been reappointed to date.
The Faculty Senate was authorized in 1960 by the general faculty to conduct any business assigned to the faculty by law or by the Rhode Island Board of Educ ation/Council on Postsecondary Education and now by the Board of Trustees.

Becky Hill, Vice President for Human Resources Becky Hill joined the University of Rhode Island in October 2024 as its inaugural Vice President for Human Resources.

Prior to URI, she served as Associate Vice President for Human Resources at Cornell University, where she provided strategic leadership and oversaw various HR functions, including information systems, benefits administration, labor relations, workforce planning, and policy compliance.
During her eight -year tenure at Cornell, Ms.
Hill held several positions of increasing responsibility, including Director of Human Resources for eCornell and Interim Senior Director of Program Delivery for eCornell, managing the delivery of academic microcredentials to over 110,000 students annually.
Before her time at Cornell, she worked as a global personnel specialist and outreach coordinator with IMB.
Ms.
Hill earned a Bachelor of Fine Arts degree from Syracuse University, an executive master's degree in human resources management from Cornell, and an eCornell certificate in human resources.
She is an active member of the Society for Human Resource Management and has a strong record of community service, including board positions with the SUNY Cortland Child Care Center and Hospicare and Palliative Care.
At URI, Ms.

Hill is responsible for developing and directing a strategic vision for human resources, aiming to foster an inclusive and supportive workplace culture that aligns with the University's mission and strategic plan.

Previously, VP Miner served as assistant dean of career services and outreach at the U niversity of Detroit Mercy School of Law.
She practiced as a commercial litigator in Dickinson Wright PLLC’s Detroit office, where she was an inaugural member of the firm’s diversity committee and co-authored the firm’s diversity mission statement.
She also clerked for the Honorable Anna Diggs Taylor of the U.S.

District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan.
She earned a Bachelor of Arts degree, magna cum laude, from Mount Holyoke College, where she currently serves on the Board of Trustees and on the board’s diversity, equity, and inclusion task force.
She earned a Juris Doctor degree from the University of Michigan Law School.
VP Miner has been active in several bar and community organizations, including selection to the American Bar Association’s To rt, Trial, and Insurance Practice Section Leadership Academy; the State Bar of Michigan’s Character and Fitness Committee; and as one of Michigan Lawyers Weekly’s Women in the Law.
She has served on the Board of Trustees for the Women Lawyers Association o f Michigan Foundation and the Board of Directors for Alternatives for Girls.
Ellen M.
Reynolds, Vice President Student Affairs Ellen Reynolds was appointed Vice President of Student Affairs by President Parlange in March 2022.
She oversees Campus Recreation, Campus Stores, Counseling Center, Dean of Students, Dining Services, Housing and Residential Life, Health Services, Memorial Student Union, Center for Student Leadership and Talent Development.

A-7 exceeding $100 million and a staff of more than 300.

Matthew McDonald, Vice President for Communications and Marketing Matthew McDonald was appointed to the newly established position of Vice President for Communications and Marketing in August 2022 to advance the mission and global reputation of the University of Rhode Island.
As the senior communications administrator at URI, Mr.

McDonald provides strategic leadership for the development and implementation of data -informed marketing and communications strategies that engage the University’s many audiences and advance URI’s reputation locally, nationally, and internationally.

McDonald served as associate vice president for communications at the University of Miami from February 2018 to July 2022.

McDonald worked at Northeastern University from 2009 to 2018, serving in athletics, development, and external affairs, and advancing to the position of assistant vice president for communications.

Alyssa V.
Boss, General Counsel Alyssa V.
Boss, Esq. was appointed as General Counsel in July of 2021.

Boss was a partner in the law firm of Cameron & Mittleman LLP in Providence, Rhode Island.

Boss worked for Care New England Health System, rising from Associate Vice President and General Counsel to the position of Executive Vice President and General Counsel.

Thorr Bjorn, Director of Athletics Thorr Bjorn was appointed Director of Athletics in August of 2007.

Bjorn has more than 30 years of experience working Division I Athletics.

Bjorn completed a four -year term as the Football Championship Subdivision (“ FCS”) Football Selection Committee Chairman.
